page: Microsoft Azure D16nds_v6 is a network-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dndv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, offering 16 dedicated vCPUs. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

For local storage requirements, the D16nds_v6 includes a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD. The server is also premium storage capable, allowing integration with high-performance external storage volumes. It does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses. This configuration lacks a dedicated GPU, making it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated graphics or parallel computing workloads.

From a resource density perspective, the D16nds_v6 provides a balanced allocation of compute and memory alongside fast local NVMe storage. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring a mix of processing power and local disk performance without the overhead of GPU hardware. Appropriate workloads include general-purpose applications, relational databases, network-optimized services, and mid-tier application servers.
description: The Microsoft Azure D16nds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine from the Dndv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Storage capabilities include a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable for external disk expansion. It does not feature a GPU or include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Designed with network optimization in mind, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring balanced compute, memory, and fast local storage. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, database hosting, and network-intensive services.
